evidence.observation: Single source of truth for the three memory-kernel header names used on both the inbound panel edge and the outbound kernel call: META_HEADER_SERVICE_ID = 'x-tdai-service-id' (instance selector), META_HEADER_USER_KEY = 'x-tdai-user-key' (caller identity) and META_HEADER_REQUEST_ID = 'x-request-id' (correlation id). Both validate-panel-headers.ts (inbound) and transport-fetch.ts (outbound) import these same constants, so the accepted request headers can never drift from the headers the panel forwards to the kernel.

Hono middleware factory mounted on every credential-bearing panel route (/meta/*, /skill/*, /chat-memory/*, /knowledge/*, /task/*, /agent/*). It derives the action from the path via readAction, requires x-tdai-service-id (META_HEADER_SERVICE_ID) and resolves it through deps.instanceRegistry, returning respondControlError 400 MISSING_INSTANCE_ID / INVALID_INSTANCE on failure. It then requires x-tdai-user-key (META_HEADER_USER_KEY) unless the action is 'auth/verify' (400 MISSING_USER_KEY), and finally publishes the normalized 'panelMeta' context variable {instanceId, gatewayEndpoint, gatewayApiKey, userKey} that route handlers copy into a MetaCallContext. This is the gate that turns raw HTTP request headers into kernel credentials.

Declares the per-request credential bundle stored under c.set('panelMeta', ...): instanceId, gatewayEndpoint, gatewayApiKey and optional userKey. These are exactly the fields routes copy into MetaCallContext and that toKernelCredentials later maps to outbound endpoint/apiKey/userKey.

Slices the kernel action suffix after the '/meta/' marker of the request path, returning '' when the marker is absent. Because /skill/* paths yield '' (never 'auth/verify'), the reuse of this middleware on the skill proxy forces x-tdai-user-key to be present, matching the skill data-plane requirement for owner identity.

Registers api.post('/meta/*', validatePanelMetaHeaders(deps), handler): the handler reads the action, rejects not-in-scope/unknown actions, builds MetaCallContext {instanceId, gatewayEndpoint, gatewayApiKey, userKey, reqId} from panelMeta + c.get('reqId'), optionally performs a duplicate check, then forwards to deps.metaKernel.invoke(action, body, ctx) and returns the kernel envelope through respondEnvelope. This is the canonical route -> adapter hand-off point.

Meta adapter: sanitizes the body (drops top-level limit/offset for non-list actions), flags omitUserKey for action 'auth/verify', converts the MetaCallContext into KernelCredentials via toKernelCredentials, then calls this.http.postEnvelope(`/v3/meta/${action}`, payload, cred). It maps an abstract action name to the concrete kernel /v3/meta/* path.

Maps the request-scoped MetaCallContext plus the configured timeout into KernelCredentials {endpoint: gatewayEndpoint, apiKey: gatewayApiKey, instanceId, userKey, timeoutMs, requestId}; when opts.omitUserKey is set (auth/verify) the user key is dropped. This is the adapter-to-transport bridge that decides which identity material is forwarded.

KernelHttpPort implementation: delegates to executeMetaFetch({endpoint, apiKey, serviceId: instanceId, userKey, timeoutMs, requestId, logger}, path, body, 'envelope'), so business code!=0 responses pass through as envelopes instead of throwing. On KernelFetchError it synthesizes a MetaEnvelope with code 504 -> message KERNEL_TIMEOUT or 502 -> KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE, guaranteeing callers always receive an envelope shape.

Outbound transport: builds the header map using the constants from headers.ts (Content-Type, [META_HEADER_SERVICE_ID]=serviceId, [META_HEADER_REQUEST_ID]=reqId, Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>, optional [META_HEADER_USER_KEY]), POSTs JSON to `${endpoint}${path}` with an AbortController timeout, parses the raw kernel envelope and normalizes it to MetaEnvelope {code, message, request_id, data}. In 'envelope' mode non-zero codes are returned rather than thrown (transparent proxy); timeout/network failures become KernelFetchError(504/502).

Defines the kernel envelope contract {code, message, request_id, data} that every adapter returns and every route responds with; request_id carries the correlation id aligned with the x-request-id header.
Envelope-to-HTTP status mapping used on the response edge: 0 -> 200, 400-599 -> the code itself, anything else -> 502. This is how a kernel business code becomes the HTTP status seen by the browser.

Response helper that serializes a MetaEnvelope as JSON with the status produced by mapHttpStatusFromEnvelopeCode; respondControlError (22-25) wraps controlEnvelope(code, message, c.get('reqId')) through the same path, so header-validation failures and kernel responses share one response contract.

Skill data-plane adapter: same credential mapping as the meta adapter but always forwards userKey (no auth/verify exception) and posts to `/v3/skill/${action}` with the body untouched (skill pagination is nested). Shows the shared-credential / different-kernel-path branch of the flow.

Knowledge-service branch of the same credential model: sends Content-Type, Authorization: Bearer <authToken> and x-tdai-service-id = instanceId, then parses the CoreEnvelope; non-zero code throws CoreUpstreamError (mapped to a control envelope by runKs in routes/knowledge/common.ts), demonstrating that the service-id header identity is reused across kernel and KS callers.

Composes the panel app: installs requestLogger on all paths (correlation id), registers health, meta-proxy, skill-proxy, chat-memory, task, agent and knowledge routes under /api/v1, and defines the onError handler that emits the same {code, message, request_id, data} envelope with code 500. This is the entry point of the diagrammed request flow.

Wiring that gives the diagram its concrete objects: a single FetchKernelHttpAdapter (KernelHttpPort) shared by FetchMetaKernelAdapter and FetchSkillKernelAdapter, plus a knowledgeClientFactory that stamps each HttpKnowledgeClient with the resolved instanceId as x-tdai-service-id. Explains how the abstract `deps.metaKernel`/`deps.skillKernel` in routes become real adapters.

claims.claim: headers.ts is the single source of truth for the three memory-kernel header names: META_HEADER_SERVICE_ID ('x-tdai-service-id'), META_HEADER_USER_KEY ('x-tdai-user-key') and META_HEADER_REQUEST_ID ('x-request-id'); the same constants are imported by the inbound validation middleware and the outbound fetch transport, so inbound header parsing and outbound header emission cannot diverge.

validatePanelMetaHeaders gates every credential-bearing panel route: readAction derives the action from the path, x-tdai-service-id must be present and resolvable in the InstanceRegistry (else 400 MISSING_INSTANCE_ID / INVALID_INSTANCE), x-tdai-user-key is required unless the action is 'auth/verify' (else 400 MISSING_USER_KEY), and the resolved entry is published as the panelMeta context variable {instanceId, gatewayEndpoint, gatewayApiKey, userKey} for downstream adapters.

Route handlers build a MetaCallContext ({instanceId, gatewayEndpoint, gatewayApiKey, userKey, reqId}) from the panelMeta variable plus the requestLogger correlation id and hand it to a kernel adapter (deps.metaKernel.invoke for /meta/*, deps.skillKernel.invoke for /skill/*); the adapter maps that context to outbound KernelCredentials via toKernelCredentials, dropping the user key only for auth/verify.

Adapters delegate to KernelHttpPort.postEnvelope, implemented by FetchKernelHttpAdapter, which calls executeMetaFetch; the transport attaches x-tdai-service-id, x-request-id, Authorization: Bearer <api_key> and the optional x-tdai-user-key, POSTs to {endpoint}/v3/<surface>/<action>, and normalizes the kernel response into a MetaEnvelope {code, message, request_id, data}, even converting transport failures into 504 KERNEL_TIMEOUT / 502 KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE envelopes.

On the response edge, handlers return the envelope through respondEnvelope, which serializes it as JSON using mapHttpStatusFromEnvelopeCode (0 -> 200, 400-599 -> code, otherwise 502); pre-adapter failures such as missing headers route through respondControlError into the identical envelope shape, so the whole flow from HTTP route to adapter to envelope terminates in one response contract.

Knowledge routes reuse the same header gate (validatePanelMetaHeaders) but reach the knowledge service through HttpKnowledgeClient.post, which sends Authorization: Bearer <authToken> plus x-tdai-service-id = instanceId and throws CoreUpstreamError on non-zero envelope codes; routes/knowledge/common.ts runKs maps that error into a control envelope, confirming the service-id identity header is the common thread across kernel and KS branches.

conclusion: The MemoryPanel request flow is a header-driven, single-envelope pipeline. A browser/SDK POST enters buildPanelApp in MemoryPanel/src/panel/http/app.ts, where requestLogger assigns/reuses x-request-id. Every credential-bearing route (/meta/*, /skill/*, /chat-memory/*, /knowledge/*, /task/*, /agent/*) is guarded by validatePanelMetaHeaders (MemoryPanel/src/panel/http/middleware/validate-panel-headers.ts). That middleware is the single inbound normalizer: it extracts the action from the path, reads x-tdai-service-id and x-tdai-user-key (names defined once in MemoryPanel/src/panel/kernel/headers.ts), resolves the instance to gatewayEndpoint + api_key via InstanceRegistry, exempts the 'auth/verify' action from the user-key requirement, and publishes panelMeta for handlers. Handlers assemble a MetaCallContext (plus the requestLogger reqId) and invoke a kernel adapter: FetchMetaKernelAdapter -> /v3/meta/{action} for metadata, FetchSkillKernelAdapter -> /v3/skill/{action} for skills, or HttpKnowledgeClient -> /v3/wiki|cod-graph for knowledge. Adapters convert the context to KernelCredentials (toKernelCredentials) and delegate to KernelHttpPort.postEnvelope, implemented by FetchKernelHttpAdapter, which runs executeMetaFetch: it re-emits the very same header constants outbound (x-tdai-service-id, x-request-id, Authorization: Bearer, optional x-tdai-user-key), POSTs JSON, and normalizes the reply into a MetaEnvelope {code, message, request_id, data}. Handlers finally return that envelope through respondEnvelope, which maps envelope.code to HTTP status (0->200, 400-599->code, else 502); pre-adapter failures use respondControlError and produce the identical envelope, so the route -> adapter -> envelope contract is uniform. See the 'diagram' field for the full ASCII request-flow diagram from HTTP route to adapter to envelope.

validation.command: python3 - <<'PY' (static checks: JSON parse; task_id==15, repository=='tdam', mode=='explore'; required evidence paths present; each evidence start_line<=symbol line range<=end_line by reading the cited files and confirming the named symbol appears within the inclusive range; each claim's evidence_paths non-empty and resolvable)
validation.notes: Runtime/build validation was not possible in-workspace: MemoryPanel/node_modules is absent and dependencies must not be installed, so `npm run typecheck` (tsc) and `npm test` (vitest) could not be executed. Validation therefore used static checks: (1) result.json parsed as JSON; (2) task_id/repository/mode verified against the current TASK.md; (3) the two contract files MemoryPanel/src/panel/kernel/headers.ts and MemoryPanel/src/panel/http/middleware/validate-panel-headers.ts each have an evidence entry whose inclusive line range contains its named symbol (verified by reading the files); (4) all cited path/line ranges were re-read and the named symbols confirmed present; (5) every claim lists at least one existing evidence_path. Limitation: no compiler/vitest execution because the optional test dependency tree is unavailable and installing it is out of scope.
